title: Data Management and Analysis at the National Center for Electron Microscopy
content: In electron microscopy, images are both the mode in which data is acquired and the means by which data is visualized and communicated. In materials science, the modes are diverse: real space, reciprocal space, spectral; the length scales are diverse: angstrom to micron and nanoparticles to bulk materials; and the materials of interest are diverse: inorganic, organic and composites. Workflows tend to be different for each use case, and often a specific TEM is chosen for a given detector or workflow. Unlike the mature field of single particle cryoEM, different workflows result in diverse data structures often combining folders and file names to impart organization. But the goal is the same: acquire and store data with sufficient labeling such that established protocols can be used to produce the final research products (figures and text) to communicate the results.
